actual_checks: All full exact inputs and both full prior bodies read. Earlier assembly/tori and hyperbolic/CAT0 regimes do not contain the virtually-solvable theorem; the announced dimension-4 counterexample is not used. The added regime and explicit nonabelian nilmanifold example are substantive.

Wegner supplies coefficient K- and L-theoretic assembly relative to virtually cyclic groups for every virtually solvable group. This includes all orientation-character twists. Bartels–Luck Proposition 0.3 requires torsion-free G, K bijective <=0/surjective in degree 1 and all-degree twisted L; all are supplied.

A closed aspherical manifold has finite integral cohomological dimension from its finite-dimensional contractible-cover CW model. Restricting a finite projective resolution to a prime-order subgroup contradicts its unbounded periodic integral cohomology, proving torsion-freeness. The surgery criterion concerns the marked structure set, so each specified equivalence is homotopic to a homeomorphism, not merely existence of some homeomorphism.

Heisenberg multiplication and integer subgroup closure, central commutator xy-prime-x-prime*y, proper free lattice action and compact coordinate-reduction domain are checked. H is R3; product with T^k for k>=2 gives closed aspherical dimension 3+k>=5 and a nonabelian solvable group. No smooth-rigidity, general dimension-4 or arbitrary-group assertion follows.
